study_identification_part.si_4_title: Neuroanatomical heterogeneity and homogeneity in individuals at clinical high risk for psychosis

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study used the ENIGMA CHR-P (Enhancing NeuroImaging Genetics through Meta-Analysis - Clinical High Risk for Psychosis) consortium dataset, which amalgamated clinical and neuroimaging data from 29 international sites. This represents a multi-site mega-analysis dataset specifically focused on individuals at clinical high risk for psychosis.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "The ENIGMA CHR-P dataset amalgamated clinical and neuroimaging data from 29 sites, comprising 1579 individuals meeting CHR-P criteria... and 1243 HC participants."

answer.ENIGMA-CHR-P (CHR-P subset): test set for normative comparison and heterogeneity assessment

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The study used a normative modelling approach where the healthy control (HC) group served as the normative reference. The Person-Based Similarity Index (PBSI) was calculated by correlating each CHR-P individual's neuroanatomical profiles with the profiles of HC members. The resulting PBSI scores represent the degree of deviation from the 'normative' range. A threshold of >1.5 SD was used to identify CHR-P individuals with marked deviation from the normative neuroanatomical profile.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "Normative reference: Next, the respective neuroanatomical profiles of each CHR-P individual were correlated with the corresponding profiles of the members of the HC group, for each brain phenotype. The resulting PBSI scores thus represent the degree of deviation from the 'normative' range and were transformed into z-scores (PBSI-CT-Z, PBSI-SA-Z, and PBSI-SV-Z). We set >1.5 SD as a threshold to identify individuals at CHR-P who most markedly deviated from the normative neuroanatomical profile"
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Baldwin2022.pdf.md: Methods / Person-Based Similarity Index, L106-L107

model-1.model-name: PBSI normative reference model (Surface Area, Cortical Thickness, Subcortical Volume)

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: This study used a reference-based normative approach rather than a traditional train/test split. The 1243 healthy controls served as the normative reference population, against which CHR-P individuals' neuroanatomical profiles were compared. The PBSI method correlates each individual's brain measures with the brain measures of members of the reference sample (HC group). There was no separate training phase; the entire HC sample served as the normative reference.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "Following quality control procedures (eFig. 1), the final sample consisted of 1579 CHR-P participants (mean age = 20.63 [SD = 4.60], 47.37% females) and 1243 HC participants (mean age = 22.32 [SD = 4.96], 44.73% females) across 29 sites."

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The age statistics are reported for the healthy control (HC) group which served as the normative reference population. Mean age was 22.32 years with SD of 4.96 years. Min, max, median, and IQR were not reported. Since this is a reference-based normative approach without a separate training phase, the train-phase statistics are not applicable.
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: "the final sample consisted of... 1243 HC participants (mean age = 22.32 [SD = 4.96], 44.73% females) across 29 sites."

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The sex distribution for the healthy control (HC) group serving as the normative reference was 687 males and 556 females, representing 55.27% male and 44.73% female. The percentages were calculated from the raw counts (687/1243 = 55.27% male; 556/1243 = 44.73% female). Since this is a reference-based normative approach without a separate training phase, the train-phase statistics are not applicable.
